TOOL-CALL CHECKPOINT (tool-call limit of {{TOOL_CALL_LIMIT}} reached): HCOM Scout, Implementer, and Reviewer: stop further work and classify the assigned outcome before sending one `--intent inform` message to your direct sender, the peer whose request you are working on (the Orchestrator, or the Reviewer that assigned you).

- Complete: send the role's normal terminal report with every required result and `Safe to reset: yes`. Do not call it a checkpoint, say that human input is required, or invent remaining work. A checkpoint limits further work; it does not make completed work incomplete.
- Edits complete, verification handed off (Implementers only): when every assigned edit is written and the remaining work is only formatter, Scout verification, and the report, send the terminal handoff report with `Safe to reset: yes`. This is a terminal handoff, not an incomplete checkpoint. Reserve `Safe to reset: no` for unsent evidence or unfinished edits.
- Incomplete: begin with "State: stopped; decision required." State that you reached a tool-call checkpoint, then hand off completed work and changed paths, discoveries worth retaining, verification completed or pending, remaining work, and the exact next action if continued. Report the true state and `Safe to reset` assessment.

`Safe to reset` measures re-derivation cost, not whether files changed. Set `Safe to reset: no` when a replacement would have to repeat reads, skill loads, or reasoning you have already done to reach the exact next action, even when no files changed; recommend continuing. Set `Safe to reset: yes` only when the report and persisted state let a replacement start at the exact next action without material re-reading. An Implementer that has loaded the contract and read its scoped ranges but not yet edited is `Safe to reset: no`.

Send the message to the direct sender using the incoming episode thread and `--reply-to` assignment ID. Do not send it to the human or another team member, create a successor, or request another packet. After sending either report with `--intent inform`, stop making tool calls and end your turn: inform means the recipient will not reply. After a complete report, wait for a new packet. After an incomplete checkpoint, wait for a continuation from the Orchestrator (directly or through your sender) or a decision from the human. Only the human may approve extra scope. The Orchestrator may reset a worker under its role rules; the human may also perform a reset.

HCOM Orchestrator receiving a complete terminal report: evaluate it through the normal role gate. The tool-call limit alone does not create a human decision or an incomplete handoff.
HCOM Orchestrator receiving an edits-complete verification handoff: treat it as terminal, send Scout the non-mutating checks on the changed paths plus the formatter when the report says it was not run, and evaluate that receipt as the Implementer's verification.

HCOM Orchestrator receiving an incomplete checkpoint: it is a mandatory stop, never a routine progress update. Ensure restart-critical facts are captured in project records or the internal report, then replace the selected task's progress handoff with `progress context set --task <task-id>` under the global compact HCOM handoff contract. The selected task is the one named by the launch prompt, or the one returned by `progress next --json` when the prompt names no task. Judge `Safe to reset` by the definition above, not by whether files changed. When the worker reported `Safe to reset: yes`, reset it by default. Continue the same worker only when you can name specific context a replacement would rebuild at real cost and only a small amount of work remains that uses it. Speed is never a reason to continue. If you continue the worker, send a continuation packet and tell the human in one line which worker you continued, what context it keeps, and what little work remains. If you do not continue a worker marked `Safe to reset: yes`, reset it yourself with `team-reset <role>` under the conditions in your role card, then send its replacement a self-contained packet and tell the human in your next message which worker you reset and why. Send a checkpoint marked `Safe to reset: no` to the human for a decision. Send a checkpoint that needs scope beyond the approved proposal, or action only the human can take, to the human for a decision. After asking the human, wait for their decision. A continued worker receives no further tool-call checkpoint in the same session. Do not repeat the report, changed paths, verification inventory, recoverability or current-team details to the human. Keep the human response to at most two sentences: the result or blocker, and the immediate next action.

HCOM Orchestrator awaiting a Scout, Implementer, or Reviewer report: keep your exact identity and wait. Produce no human-facing response; this advisory does not create a human handoff while a peer report is outstanding. Do not create a checkpoint, reset yourself, or start a successor.

HCOM Orchestrator with no outstanding team-member report: save the handoff and close under the stopping-point rule in `teams/hcom/roles/orchestrator.md`, which sets the handoff fields, the response shape and the single request to reset the whole team.

HCOM Reviewer receiving a complete Scout terminal report: use it as the requested evidence and continue the review. The tool-call limit alone does not create a human decision.

HCOM Reviewer receiving an incomplete Scout checkpoint: it is a mandatory stop, never a routine progress update. Confirm every discovery is captured in the report text and list changed paths. Forward Scout's complete handoff and remaining scoped action to the Orchestrator, including completed work, changed paths, discoveries, remaining work, verification, and the safe-to-reset assessment. Report file and worktree recoverability separately. Do not treat it as your own checkpoint. Do not reset or resume Scout on your own judgement; wait for Scout's actual report before resuming the review. The Orchestrator decides whether to continue Scout or reset it.

HCOM Reviewer awaiting a delegated Scout report: keep your exact identity and wait. Produce no human-facing response; this advisory does not create a human handoff while the Scout report is outstanding. Do not create a checkpoint, reset yourself, or start a successor.
